title: Developer tryflow & economic anchors — quick messaging + ops snippets
summary: Compact messaging brief and tactical copy for a 60–120s developer tryflow and pricing anchors that emphasize cost clarity and production-readiness. Includes experiment ideas, objection responses, and short SDK snippets for landing pages and onboarding emails.
body:
Purpose:
- Create a short, testable set of developer-first copy and quickstart steps that convert trial signups into first API calls and then first production route. Emphasize predictability (latency/cost), low time-to-value, and safe experimentation (free credits + guardrails).

Audience:
- Primary: software engineers and ML engineers evaluating an inference API for product integration (chat, generation, embeddings).
- Secondary: platform/product leads who will champion adoption inside their org.

Core positioning (single-sentence):
- "Redwood Inference: get accurate LLM responses that cost less and ship faster — same API from prototype to SLA-backed production."

Three developer-first value props (headlines + 1-line amplifiers):
1) "From zero to sample in 60s" — Starter SDKs and curated quickstarts that produce a working call in under a minute with copy-and-paste examples and test prompts.
2) "Predictable cost, visible metrics" — Per-token breakdowns, per-route cost estimates, and commit options that let engineers forecast the bill before scaling.
3) "Same API for sandbox and SLA" — Pin a model version, switch routing policies later, and keep the integration unchanged when you graduate to Dedicated or Private.

Quickstart tryflow (target: first API call within 60–90s) — copy for landing page + onboarding email + console: 
- Landing CTA: "Try a working example in 60s" -> opens inline modal with 3 steps.
- Step 1 (1 line): Sign up (email + GitHub) — you get $50 credit for 30 days.
- Step 2 (code): Copy-paste minimal snippet:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"rm-1-small","prompt":"Summarize this: We launched...","max_tokens":60}'
- Step 3 (observe): See token cost estimate and latency under the response. Button: "Save this route" to create an API route and lock a model version.

Inline quick copy variants (for A/B tests):
- Variant A headline: "Ship LLM features faster, keep costs down."
- Variant B headline: "High-throughput LLMs with developer SDKs and transparent pricing."

Pricing language drafts (short and long forms):
- Minimal (homepage): "Pay-as-you-go: Usage-based pricing with free trial credits. Transparent per-token breakdowns in the console."
- Developer-focused (onboard email): "Your free $50 credit covers ~100K tokens on rm-1-small. Check per-request estimates in the console to see exact cost before you send."
- Enterprise-facing line (early stage): "Reserve capacity for predictable throughput — custom pricing and SLAs available for Dedicated and Private deployments."

Economic anchors (words + numeric examples to test):
- Anchor 1 (latency): "Median 95ms token latency for common prompts (under 1k seq) — see perf page."
- Anchor 2 (cost): "Typical chat: 1–3 cents per response for most app patterns (demo numbers, adjust by model)."
- Anchor 3 (scale): "Autoscaling bursts + reserved pools — scale without rewriting integration."

Competitive differentiator notes (to use in internal objection handling):
- Versus hyperscale cloud managed endpoints: emphasize unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, explicit cost per token, and inference-first SLOs rather than generic endpoint management.
- Versus model-only APIs: call out routing/fallback policies and caching to save unit costs at production scale.
- Versus open-source self-hosted runtimes: highlight developer experience (SDKs, metrics, rollouts) + optional private deployments for compliance.

Short objection scripts (for SEs / chat):
- "Your pricing is unpredictable" -> "We provide per-route cost estimates and a token-level cost breakdown so you can validate expected spend before scaling. We also offer reserved capacity to cap per-hour spend."
- "We need on-prem/on-VPC" -> "Same API and tooling works for Private deployments; we can walk you through a pilot and audit KMS/HSM integrations."
- "I need faster inference" -> "We publish performance profiles per model and recommend config/quantization guidance; we can run a short workload test to suggest changes."

Homepage/hero microcopy options (test these 3):
- Option 1: "Ship LLM features that scale — predictable cost, one API for dev to production."
- Option 2: "Build fast, pay predictably — developer-first inference with built-in observability."
- Option 3: "Start with a sample in 60s. Upgrade to SLA-backed capacity as you grow."

Console CTA copy and microflows (to reduce friction):
- Primary CTA: "Create demo route" -> preselects rm-1-small, returns a curl snippet and shows estimated cost for the next 100 tokens.
- Secondary CTA: "Run workload test" -> uploads sample prompt set and returns throughput/cost profile within minutes.

Outbound email subject + body snippets (for trial activation):
- Subject A: "You’ve got $50 — try a live inference in 60s"
- Body intro: "Hey <name>, your trial credit is ready. Copy this curl and see a live response + cost estimate in your console. Reply if you want a quick workload smoke test."

Short SDK snippet (JS) to include in quickstarts: 
- const redwood = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
  const resp = await redwood.generate({ model: 'rm-1-small', prompt: 'Extract 3 bullets from: ...', max_tokens: 80 });
  console.log(resp.text);

Suggested A/B experiments (priority order):
1) CTA wording on landing page: "60s" vs "1 minute" vs "Get started" (measure click-through -> console create).
2) Pricing anchor in console: show per-request estimate vs only per-token post-bill (measure conversion to first API call).
3) Free credit size: $25 vs $50 vs $100 (measure % who hit commit route).

Operational snippets for SEs (copyable):
- Quick demo checklist (2 min): 1) Create route with rm-1-small, 2) Run 10 sample prompts from our demo set, 3) Show token breakdown and latency tab, 4) Offer to run a 3-minute throughput test.
- Pilot kickoff email (copy): "Hi <name>, excited to pilot Redwood. I’ve provisioned a demo route and $50 credit. When’s a 20-minute window to run a 5–10k token throughput test?"

Metrics to track during rollout (product + GTM):
- Activation funnel: signup -> console arrived -> first API call -> create route
- Time metrics: median time signup->first-call, signup->route-create
- Cost/usage: median tokens per first-call, % of users who view per-request estimate before calling
- Revenue signals: % trialers who convert to paid, MRR from early small customers

Open questions / risks we should test: 
- Does explicit per-request cost estimation increase or decrease developer experimentation?
- Which economic anchor (latency vs $/response) drives faster internal championing?
- How many developers prefer CLI/curl quickstarts vs SDK examples on first-run?

Next steps (owners):
- Product: expose per-request estimator in the inline quickstart modal (owner: Maya).
- DevRel: implement A/B test for landing CTA wording (owner: Aisha).
- SE Playbook: roll this quick demo checklist into standard pilot kit and share as a ready-to-send email (owner: Leo).

Notes / links to collateral:
- Performance benchmarks page (draft): LINK_CONFLUENCE_PERF
- Example quickstart repo: github:repo/redwood/quickstarts#js-simple

Stretch copy ideas (for later experiments):
- "Predictable inference: ship features, not infrastructure."
- "One integration, endless deployment choices."

---
End of brief.
